parts:
Dear all,

I am implementing a kind of N-mixture model with three parts:

1- multinomial model for double-observer data to estimate detection probability;

2- binomial model for replicate days (J=2);

3- Poisson model for abundance;

Nevertheless, I do not have a complete dataset: ng.cor (matrix of number of groups detected only by observer 1, only by observer 2 and by both observers) is partly completed and partly missed because I was only able to implement double-platform in two from five months.
Thus, in the cases where ng.cor[,1:3] is complete I use dmulti, and in the cases where ng.cor[,1:3] is not complete I just use a binomial distribution. That is why you will see four loops (two for each replicate - day) instead of only one.
 
When running this model I am getting the error regarding ng.cor2[1, 1:3]: "node inconsistent with parents".
I have already tried to change trials ngroups2 (to ngroups2 + 2 and + 5 and so on) and also N.compl (binomial model) and Ng (Poisson model).

Code are below and data can be downloaded here (Dropbox link):
https://www.dropbox.com/sh/1p9fidw1g4x702f/AACgJuaLuIg6IvbR_Klqjt9Ca?dl=0

I appreciate any suggestion.
Thank you a lot.

Best,
Heloise

#--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Density and abundance estimate from repeated counts 
#--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Entry for Jags
load('dataC.inia.rda')
dimnames(dataC.inia)
str(dataC.inia)

load('rep1C.rda')
dimnames(rep1C)
str(rep1C)

load('rep2C.rda')
dimnames(comb_rep2C)
str(comb_rep2C)

# Number of detection per obs (front=obs1, back=obs2) and replicate
n1 <- data.frame(rep1C$replicate, rep1C$ngroups.obs1, rep1C$ngroups.obs2, rep1C$ngroups.both, NA)
n2 <- data.frame(comb_rep2C$replicate, comb_rep2C$ngroups.obs1, comb_rep2C$ngroups.obs2, comb_rep2C$ngroups.both, NA)
names(n1) <- c('rep', 'obs1', 'obs2', 'both', 'nd')
names(n2) <- c('rep', 'obs1', 'obs2', 'both', 'nd')

# To separate only samples with detections by front and back platforms (obs1 and 2, feb and jun)
# f1.cor and f2.cor are indexes that represent only double-platform data for day (k) 1 and 2.
# f1.on and f2.on are indexes that represent only sightings of observer 1 (front platform).
# The final object is a data.frame
i1 <- 1:nrow(n1)
f1c <- i1[n1$both >= 0]
f1.cor <- as.numeric(na.omit(f1c))
f1.on <- as.numeric(attributes(na.omit(f1c))$na.action)

i2 <- 1:nrow(n2)
f2c <- i2[n2$both >= 0]
f2.cor <- as.numeric(na.omit(f2c))
f2.on <- as.numeric(na.omit(i2[n2$obs1 >= 0 & is.na(n2$both) == TRUE]))

# Initializing ngroups replicates and N
ngroups1 <- as.numeric(apply(n1, 1, max, na.rm = T))
ngroups2 <- as.numeric(apply(n2, 1, max, na.rm = T))
ngroups <- data.matrix(cbind(ngroups1, ngroups2))
ngroups.cor <- apply(ngroups, 1, max, na.rm = T)
N.compl <- cbind(ngroups1 + 2, ngroups2 + 2) # max from n1 and n2 + 2
# (jags does not accept data.frames as initial values)

# Data list for jags
ng.cor1 <- as.matrix(n1[f1.cor, 2:5])
ng.cor2 <- as.matrix(n2[f2.cor, 2:5])
ng1 <- n1[f1.on, 2]
ng2 <- n2[f2.on, 2]

data.list <- list(T = nrow(n1),
                  K = 2,
                  F1 = length(f1.cor),
                  J1 = length(f1.on),
                  F2 = length(f2.cor),
                  J2 = length(f2.on),
                  ng.cor1 = ng.cor1,
                  ng1 = ng1,
                  ng.cor2 = ng.cor2, 
                  ng2 = ng2,
                  f1.cor = f1.cor,
                  f1.on = f1.on,
                  f2.cor = f2.cor,
                  f2.on = f2.on)
                  #rstate = cbind(rep1C$rstate + 1, comb_rep2C$rstate + 1),
                  #rain = cbind(rep1C$rain, comb_rep2C$rain),
                  #effort = cbind(rep1C$effort, comb_rep2C$effort))

# Parameters to be monitored
params <- c('p1', 'p2', 'pd', 'p.em', 'lambda', 'Ng')#, 'a0', 'a1', 'a2')

# MCMC inits
inits <- function(){ list(p1 = runif(1), p2 = runif(1),
                          ngroups1 = ngroups1[f1.cor], ngroups2 = ngroups2[f2.cor],
                          N.compl = N.compl,
                          #a0 = runif(1), a1 = runif(1), xrs = c(0.1,0.1,0.1),
                          #a2 = runif(2), xr = c(0.1,0.1), sigma = runif(1), mu.e = runif(1),
                          p.em = runif(1),
                          lambda = rpois(1, 4),
                          Ng = ngroups.cor + 5
                          )}

#--------------
# Model in BUGS
#--------------
sink('riverdolphin.do.txt')
cat('model {

## Priors:

  p1 ~ dunif(0,1)
  p2 ~ dunif(0,1)

  #a0 ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
  #a1 ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
  #for(i in 1:3){
  # xrs[i] ~ dunif(0,1)
 #}
  #for(i in 1:2){
  # a2[i] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
   #xr[i] ~ dunif(0,1)
 #}
  #mu.e ~ dnorm(10, 0.1)
  #sigma ~ dunif(0,20)
  #tau.e <- 1/(sigma*sigma)
  p.em ~ dunif(0,1)
  lambda ~ dunif(0,500)

## Likelihood:

## Observational process
        p[1] <- p1 * (1 - p2) # detected only by obs1
        p[2] <- (1 - p1) * p2 # detected only by obs2
        p[3] <- p1 * p2 # detected by both
        p[4] <- 1 - (p[1] + p[2] + p[3]) # non-detection probability
        pd <- 1 - p[4] # detection probability

        # multivariate probability vector for transect i (only for Feb and Jun)
        pdc[1] <- p[1] / pd
        pdc[2] <- p[2] / pd
        pdc[3] <- p[3] / pd

 for(f1 in 1:F1){ # F1: number of transects with double-platform day 1
        # f1.cor is the index of transects with double-platform (i.e., without NAs)
        ng.cor1[f1,1:3] ~ dmulti(pdc[1:3], ngroups1[f1])
        ngroups1[f1] ~ dbin(pd, N.compl[f1.cor[f1],1])
 } # f1

 for(j1 in 1:J1){ # J1: number of transects with only one observer day 1
        # f1 is the index of transects with only one observer
        ng1[j1] ~ dbin(p[1], N.compl[f1.on[j1],1])
 } # j1

  for(f2 in 1:F2){ # F2: number of transects with double-platform day 2
        # f1.cor is the index of transects with double-platform (i.e., without NAs)
        ng.cor2[f2,1:3] ~ dmulti(pdc[1:3], ngroups2[f2])
        ngroups2[f2] ~ dbin(pd, N.compl[f2.cor[f2],2])
 } # f2

 for(j2 in 1:J2){ # J2: number of transects with only one observer day 2
        # f2 is the index of transects with only one observer
        ng2[j2] ~ dbin(p[1], N.compl[f2.on[j2],2])
 } # j2

## Density process
# Emigration rate

 for(i in 1:T){ # T: number of transects
    for(k in 1:K){ # K: number of replicates (days)
        # p.em is the emigration probability
        # N.compl is the total population that uses the area
        N.compl[i,k] ~ dbin(p.em, Ng[i])
       # logit(p.em[i,k]) <- a0 + effort[i,k] + a1*rstate[i,k] + a2[rain[i,k]]
       # effort[i,k] ~ dnorm(mu.e, tau.e)
       # rstate[i,k] ~ dcat(xrs[])
       # rain[i,k] ~ dcat(xr[])
    } # k

# Groups density

        # NG is estimated for all transects (f1.cor + f1.on) and (f2.cor + f2.on)
        Ng[i] ~ dpois(lambda)

 } # i

# Mean of parameters
   #p.em.m <- mean(p.em[,])

}
')
sink()

#-----------
# Fit model
#-----------
library(jagsUI)

fit.do <- jags(data.list, inits, params, 'riverdolphin.do.txt', n.chains = 3,
          n.thin = 500, n.iter = 100000, n.burnin = 60000, parallel = T)


print(fit.do, dig = 3)
plot(fit.do)
